item.title: Outside Forward
item.description: The outside forward (also called a wing forward) plays on the left or right side of the formation. Your side stays your side — the labels inside (wall side) and openside (open-pool side) swap as the puck moves, but you always cover your half of the pool. See Forwards in the 3-3 for where to position yourself. Your partner is the wing back on your side — you support each other throughout the point.

item.title: Center Forward (Pivot)
item.description: The center forward — often called the pivot — controls the middle of the formation. In its simplest form, go to the puck wherever it is. Your job is to keep the attack moving: pass outward to the wing forwards, drop in support on drives, or link up with the wing backs when the play needs to shift direction. See Forwards in the 3-3 for the center forward’s area of responsibility and spacing from the puck.
